caloocan.info: Caloocan is a historic city known as the 'Home of the Katipunan'. It played a crucial role during the Philippine Revolution.

heritage_spots.name: Monumento (Bonifacio Monument)
heritage_spots.info: An iconic 45-foot pylon designed by Guillermo Tolentino commemorating Andres Bonifacio.

heritage_spots.name: San Roque Cathedral
heritage_spots.info: Established in 1815, it served as a spiritual center during the Spanish colonial period.

heritage_spots.name: Tandang Sora Birthplace
heritage_spots.info: The site where Melchora Aquino, the 'Mother of the Katipunan', was born.

caloocan.tips: Visit Monumento at night to see the lighting; it's perfect for photography.
caloocan.directions_template: From {user_loc}, take the LRT-1 to Monumento Station or a jeepney passing through McArthur Highway.

malabon.info: A coastal city rich in heritage houses and 17th-century architecture, often called the 'Venice of the Philippines'.

heritage_spots.name: San Bartolome Church
heritage_spots.info: Built in 1614, this Greco-Roman church is a masterpiece of Spanish colonial engineering.

heritage_spots.name: Raymundo Ancestral House
heritage_spots.info: The oldest documented heritage house in Malabon, built in 1861 with a distinct 'Bahay-na-Bato' style.

heritage_spots.name: Angel Cacnio Art Gallery
heritage_spots.info: Home to the works of a Master Painter; a hub for Malabon's local art scene.

malabon.tips: Try the Tricycle Heritage Tour for an easy way to see all these spots in one go.
malabon.directions_template: From {user_loc}, take a jeepney to Sangandaan, then transfer to a 'Malabon-Hulo' jeepney.

navotas.info: The 'Fishing Capital', Navotas holds maritime secrets and centennial religious sites.

heritage_spots.name: San Jose de Navotas Parish
heritage_spots.info: Established in 1859, it stands as a witness to the city's transformation from a fishing village to a city.

heritage_spots.name: Navotas Fisheries Port
heritage_spots.info: While industrial, it is the historical heart of the city's identity since the 1900s.

navotas.tips: Visit during the Bangus Festival (May) to see the traditional coastal celebrations.
navotas.directions_template: From {user_loc}, take a jeepney labeled 'Agora' or 'Navotas' passing through C4 road.

valenzuela.info: The 'Vibrant City', home of Dr. Pio Valenzuela.

local_routes.wawang_pulo_to_museo: Since malapit ka lang, take a jeep bound for 'Polo' or 'Malanday'. Baba ka sa Polo Church, walking distance na lang ang Museo.
local_routes.karuhatan: Take any jeep going North (Malanday). Baba sa Gen. T. De Leon or Malanday, then transfer to a Polo-bound jeep.

heritage_spots.name: Museo ni Dr. Pio Valenzuela
heritage_spots.info: The Museo ni Dr. Pio Valenzuela is a reconstructed heritage house and museum in Barangay Pariancillo Villa that stands on the original site of the revolutionary hero's ancestral home. It serves as a historical repository and commemoration showcasing the life of Dr. Pio Valenzuela, featuring personal artifacts and documents that highlight his critical role as a co-founder of the Katipunan.

heritage_spots.name: San Diego de Alcala Church
heritage_spots.info: The San Diego de Alcala Church is a historic red-brick belfry and parish located in Polo, Valenzuela, originally established by Franciscan missionaries in 1623. While the main church was largely destroyed during World War II, the surviving four-story stone bell tower remains one of the city's oldest landmarks and a significant symbol of its Spanish colonial heritage.

heritage_spots.name: Arkong Bato
heritage_spots.info: Arkong Bato Park is a historical landmark in Valenzuela City centered around a stone arch built in 1910 that originally marked the boundary between Bulacan and Rizal. This linear park features the restored monument of Katipunan hero Captain Delfin Velilla and provides a landscaped public space for residents to appreciate the city’s colonial heritage.

heritage_spots.name: Arkong Bato Park
heritage_spots.info: Arkong Bato Park in Valenzuela City is a historic linear park centered around a 1910 stone arch that once served as the provincial boundary between Bulacan and Rizal. Today, it functions as a landscaped heritage site featuring the monument of Katipunan hero Captain Delfin Velilla and provides a safe, pedestrian-friendly space for residents and tourists to explore local history.

heritage_spots.name: Polo Park
heritage_spots.info: Polo Park, also known as the Polo People’s Park, is a vibrant community space in Valenzuela City that serves as the modern counterpart to the historic San Diego de Alcala Church. This 2,500-square-meter plaza features a dancing fountain, landscaped gardens, and a dedicated memorial to the 159 local residents who died during World War II, making it a key destination for both relaxation and historical reflection.

heritage_spots.name: Valenzuela City People's Park
heritage_spots.info: The Valenzuela City People's Park is a 1.5-hectare urban green space located in Karuhatan, serving as the city's primary hub for outdoor recreation and community gatherings. It features modern amenities such as a dancing fountain, an aero-circle for fitness activities, and shaded picnic areas, all situated conveniently next to the Valenzuela City Hall complex.

heritage_spots.name: Valenzuela City Family Park
heritage_spots.info: A nature-centric space preserving varieties of century-old trees. The Valenzuela City Family Park is a 1.1-hectare nature-centric space in Karuhatan that preserves over 30 varieties of trees, including century-old mango and santol trees. It offers a more tranquil, shaded environment compared to the People's Park, featuring a children's playground, fitness equipment, and an amphitheater for community events.

heritage_spots.name: Valenzuela City Sports Park
heritage_spots.info: Located in Barangay Wawang Pulo, it is a premier athletic facility that features a professional-grade football field, an oval track, and multiple courts for basketball and volleyball. It serves as a major hub for local athletes and fitness enthusiasts, providing the community with a modern space for organized sports tournaments and recreational training.

heritage_spots.name: Valenzuela City Paw Park and Skate Park
heritage_spots.info: The Valenzuela City Paw Park and Skate Park is a specialized recreational area in Barangay Malinta that provides dedicated zones for both pet owners and extreme sports enthusiasts. The facility features a secure, fenced-off space with agility equipment for dogs and a modern concrete park with ramps and rails designed for skateboarding, BMX, and inline skating.

heritage_spots.name: Tagalag Fishing Village
heritage_spots.info: Known as the city's "best-kept secret", this eco-tourism zone features a 1.3-kilometer boardwalk where visitors can enjoy recreational fishing, bird watching, and sunset views. The village has transformed from a quiet pond area into a lively destination for "food crawls", offering numerous lakeside restaurants and cafes that serve fresh local catches like Tilapia and Bangus.

heritage_spots.name: National Shrine of Our Lady of Fatima
heritage_spots.info: This major pilgrimage site is the center of Fatima devotion in the Philippines and serves as the permanent home of the National Pilgrim Image (the "EDSA Image") used during the 1986 People Power Revolution. Its unique modern architectural design features a circular layout that keeps all worshippers close to the altar, and it was declared a tourist spot as early as 1982 due to its cultural and religious significance.

heritage_spots.name: Fatima Avenue
heritage_spots.info: Recently converted into a 250-meter pedestrianized green corridor, this avenue serves as a park-like connection between the Fatima Shrine and Museo Valenzuela. It is a popular "lifestyle strip" where residents go for jogging and outdoor dining, featuring heritage-style lighting, benches, and a food bazaar that showcases local Valenzuelano businesses.

heritage_spots.name: Polo Riverwalk
heritage_spots.info: Inspired by New York’s High Line, this 2.5-kilometer scenic esplanade was built on top of flood control structures to provide a safe space for walking, cycling, and jogging along the Polo River. The riverwalk connects several historic barangays and is designed to be pet-friendly, featuring heritage aesthetics that encourage residents to reclaim the waterfront as a public social space.

heritage_spots.name: WES Arena
heritage_spots.info: The Valenzuela City Sports, Art, and Events Arena (WES Arena) is a world-class indoor facility in Barangay Punturin designed for both major sports tournaments and community gatherings. It houses professional-grade courts for basketball, badminton, and volleyball, along with a gym and dance studio, serving as the city's premier venue for athletic development and local events.

heritage_spots.name: Museo Valenzuela
heritage_spots.info: Located in Barangay Marulas, this sprawling museum serves as a cultural hub housing an extensive collection of artifacts and memorabilia that trace the city's evolution from a Spanish-era town to a modern industrial center. Its preserved Spanish aesthetics and spacious grounds make it a popular venue for public seminars, art exhibits, and community events.

heritage_spots.name: Valenzuela City Public Library
heritage_spots.info: The city's modern, six-story public library in Malinta is a state-of-the-art facility designed to provide residents with a comfortable and high-tech environment for research and study. It features specialized sections for children and digital media, reflecting the city’s commitment to accessible education for all its "Valenzuelano" youth.

heritage_spots.name: Alvarez Park Cafe
heritage_spots.info: Located in Tagalag area, this unique "floating" cafe and restaurant offers a rustic, nautical dining experience right on the water. It is a popular destination for families and cyclists who want to enjoy a relaxing breakfast or dinner with a view of the local fishing grounds.

heritage_spots.name: Kamayan sa Palapat
heritage_spots.info: Kamayan sa Palapat is a classic Filipino family restaurant in the Tagalag Fishing Village known for its budget-friendly "boodle fight" meals and relaxing riverside kubos. It offers a nostalgic dining experience where guests can enjoy traditional favorites like bulalo and crispy pata while watching the sunset over the fishing ponds.

heritage_spots.name: Tata Celo Kainan sa Palaisdaan
heritage_spots.info: Tata Celo is a popular floating restaurant and fishing spot that features charming bamboo huts situated directly over functional fishponds. It is a favorite destination for "food crawls," offering a wide menu of fresh seafood and classic Pinoy dishes in a cozy, well-lit environment that is perfect for large family gatherings.

valenzuela.tips: Drop by the Polo Riverwalk nearby after visiting the Museum for a quiet sunset view.
valenzuela.directions_template: From {user_loc}, take a jeepney to Malanday, then a tricycle or jeep to Polo Church/Museum.

trivia.trivia: Born on July 11, 1869 and died at the age of 86 on April 6, 1956 at his home in Polo, Valenzuela. Dr. Pio Valenzuela was a Filipino physician, a prominent figure in Valenzuela and a central figure of the Philippine Revolution, best known as a member of the Katipunan’s "Triumvirate" alongside Andres Bonifacio and Emilio Jacinto. Born in Polo, Bulacan, to Francisco Valenzuela and Lorenza Alejandrino, he used his medical background and his family’s principalia status to support the secret society under the alias Dimas Ayaran. He played a pivotal role in the movement by serving as its Fiscal and managing the publication of the revolutionary newspaper Kalayaan, which was instrumental in rapidly expanding the Katipunan's membership across the country. One of his most significant historical contributions was his 1896 secret mission to Dapitan, where he disguised himself to seek the counsel of Dr. Jose Rizal regarding the start of the armed uprising. Following the revolution, Dr. Valenzuela transitioned into a prolific career in public service, becoming the first municipal president of Polo and later serving as the Governor of Bulacan from 1921 to 1925. His legacy is permanently immortalized in his hometown, which was renamed Valenzuela in 1960, and his life is commemorated at his reconstructed ancestral home in Barangay Pariancillo Villa, now a museum housing his personal memorabilia.
